# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan — 40,000 Users

## Overview

Migrate 40,000 users from the legacy billing system ("Old") to the new billing system ("New"). Both systems run concurrently throughout the rollout (dual-run architecture), with the Old system remaining live as a fallback through every migration phase and for a defined stabilization window after the final batch completes. Old system deprecation is treated as a **separate, later initiative** and is explicitly out of scope for the phases below.

---

## Pre-Rollout Gate (Phase 0 — not a migration phase, no users moved)

Before any user is migrated, the following must be true:
- Dual-write/dual-run reconciliation job passes on 100% of shadow-mode test transactions for 7 consecutive days with <0.01% mismatch rate.
- Rollback procedure (reverting a migrated account to Old as system-of-record) tested successfully on ≥50 synthetic accounts.
- Customer support and finance teams trained on New system's dispute/refund workflows.
- Legal/compliance sign-off on invoice numbering continuity and tax calculation parity between systems.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% — 800 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 0 gate fully passed AND a volunteer/internal cohort of low-ARR, non-enterprise accounts identified with no active disputes or payment failures in the prior 30 days.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts + opted-in low-risk external users (single payment method, monthly billing cycle only, no multi-currency).

**Duration:** 10 business days minimum.

**Activities:** Migrate accounts one cohort at a time (100/day max), run daily reconciliation between Old and New ledgers, manual review of every invoice generated in New for this phase.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero unresolved billing discrepancies >$1 and payment success rate in New ≥ Old's baseline rate (measured over the same window); support ticket volume attributable to billing did not increase >10% over Phase 1 pre-migration baseline.

**Population:** Broaden to include annual-billing and multi-payment-method accounts, still excluding highest-ARR enterprise accounts and any accounts with active custom contracts.

**Duration:** 15 business days, migrated in daily waves of ~650–700 users with automatic pause between waves pending overnight reconciliation results.

**Activities:** Introduce automated reconciliation alerting (not just manual review), enable customer-facing self-serve visibility into New system for migrated users, weekly finance sign-off checkpoint.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Final Batch (73% — 29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed at full duration with no halt events triggered (see Halt Metric below); cumulative discrepancy backlog across Phases 1–2 fully resolved and closed; enterprise/custom-contract accounts individually reviewed and scheduled with account owners.

**Population:** All remaining users, including enterprise, custom-contract, and multi-currency accounts, sequenced from lowest to highest complexity/ARR.

**Duration:** 20 business days, in waves capped at 2,000 users/day, with enterprise accounts migrated in the final 5 days on an individually scheduled, white-glove basis.

**Activities:** Full reconciliation automation, real-time discrepancy dashboard, dedicated support escalation queue for migration-related tickets. **The Old system remains fully operational, read/write capable, and is NOT disabled, deleted, or decommissioned at the end of this phase** — it enters a minimum 60-day stabilization/fallback window as system-of-record backup before any separate decommissioning project is even scoped.

---

## Halt Metric (Automatic Rollout Freeze)

**If, within any 24-hour rolling window during any phase, billing discrepancies (New vs. expected charge amount) affect more than 0.5% of migrated accounts, OR payment failure rate in New exceeds Old's trailing 30-day baseline by more than 2 percentage points — the rollout automatically halts, no further accounts are migrated, and Incident Commander is paged.** Resumption requires root-cause identification and a passed re-verification on a 200-account canary batch before the next wave proceeds.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing occurs during dual-run window due to both systems independently triggering charges | Implement idempotency keys and a single authoritative "charge owner" flag per account, enforced by a reconciliation service that blocks New from charging until Old's charge-lock is released | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Silent data mapping errors (e.g., proration, tax jurisdiction, currency rounding) produce incorrect invoice amounts that go unnoticed until customer complaints | Automated line-item-level reconciliation comparing Old vs New calculated amounts for every migrated invoice before it is sent, with hard block on send if variance exceeds $0.50 | Billing Data QA Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by migration-related tickets, delaying detection of the halt-metric threshold being crossed | Dedicated migration support queue with SLA-based escalation and a real-time ticket-tagging dashboard feeding directly into the halt-metric monitor | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated with incorrect custom pricing rules, causing contract breach exposure | Individual manual review and sign-off by account owner and finance for every enterprise/custom-contract account prior to migration, migrated only in Phase 3's white-glove batch | Enterprise Finance Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated account back to Old fails or causes data loss, leaving an account in an inconsistent billing state | Maintain full audit log and reversible migration transaction record for every account for 90 days; require successful rollback dry-run test before Phase 1 begins | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 3
